Mark.line: Mark presents Jesus as the Son of God, whose powerful ministry leads to his death and resurrection.
more: John the Baptist prepares the way, and Jesus begins preaching the kingdom of God in Galilee.
Jesus heals, casts out demons, teaches in parables, and calls twelve disciples while opposition grows.
At Caesarea Philippi Peter confesses him as the Christ, and Jesus begins predicting his suffering.
Jesus travels to Jerusalem, enters the city, cleanses the temple, and debates the religious leaders.
He is betrayed, tried, and crucified, and on the third day his tomb is found empty.

1.line: John baptizes Jesus, who is tempted in the wilderness, then begins preaching, calling disciples, and healing in Galilee.
more: John the Baptist preaches repentance and points to one mightier than himself.
The Spirit descends on Jesus, and a voice from heaven calls him the beloved Son.
Jesus calls Simon, Andrew, James, and John, then casts out demons and heals many, including a leper.

2.line: Jesus forgives and heals a paralyzed man, calls Levi, and answers objections about fasting and the Sabbath.
more: Friends lower the paralytic through a roof, and Jesus shows his authority to forgive sins.
Jesus eats with tax collectors and sinners, saying he came to call sinners.
He declares that the Son of Man is lord even of the Sabbath.

3.line: Jesus heals on the Sabbath, appoints the twelve apostles, and rebukes scribes who say he works by Beelzebul.
more: After he heals a withered hand, Pharisees and Herodians plot to destroy him.
Jesus warns that blasphemy against the Holy Spirit will never be forgiven.
He says that whoever does God's will is his brother, sister, and mother.

4.line: Jesus teaches the crowds in parables about the kingdom, then calms a storm on the Sea of Galilee.
more: The parable of the sower shows different responses to God's word.
Parables of the lamp, the growing seed, and the mustard seed describe the kingdom's growth.
When he stills the wind and waves, the frightened disciples ask who he is.

5.line: Jesus frees a man possessed by many demons, heals a bleeding woman, and raises Jairus' daughter from death.
more: In the region of the Gerasenes, the demons called Legion enter a herd of pigs.
The healed man is sent home to tell what the Lord has done for him.
A woman touching his garment is healed, and Jesus then raises the synagogue ruler's daughter.

6.line: Rejected at Nazareth, Jesus sends out the twelve, feeds five thousand, and walks on the sea.
more: Herod Antipas has John the Baptist beheaded at the request of Herodias' daughter.
Jesus feeds a great crowd with five loaves and two fish.
He walks on the water to his disciples and heals many at Gennesaret.

7.line: Jesus rebukes the Pharisees' human traditions, teaches that defilement comes from the heart, and heals Gentiles.
more: He says they set aside God's commandment to keep their own traditions.
A Syrophoenician woman's persistent faith leads Jesus to free her daughter from a demon.
In the Decapolis he heals a deaf man with a speech impediment.

8.line: Jesus feeds four thousand, Peter confesses him as the Christ, and Jesus foretells his death and resurrection.
more: Jesus refuses the Pharisees a sign and warns his disciples about their leaven.
He heals a blind man at Bethsaida in two stages.
Jesus rebukes Peter and teaches that followers must deny themselves and take up their cross.

9.line: Jesus is transfigured before three disciples, heals a demon-possessed boy, and teaches about true greatness.
more: On the mountain Moses and Elijah appear, and God's voice says to listen to his Son.
Jesus again predicts his death, but the disciples argue about who is greatest.
He teaches that the first must be servant of all and warns against causing others to sin.

10.line: On the way to Jerusalem, Jesus teaches about marriage, wealth, and servanthood, then heals blind Bartimaeus.
more: Jesus blesses children and tells a rich man to sell his possessions and follow him.
After a third prediction of his death, James and John ask for places of honor.
Jesus says the Son of Man came to serve and give his life as a ransom.

11.line: Jesus enters Jerusalem on a colt, curses a fig tree, cleanses the temple, and is questioned about his authority.
more: Crowds spread cloaks and branches, shouting Hosanna as he enters the city.
He drives out the money-changers, calling the temple a house of prayer for all nations.
The withered fig tree prompts teaching on faith, prayer, and forgiveness.

12.line: In the temple Jesus answers challenges from religious leaders and teaches about God's commandments and his own identity.
more: The parable of the wicked tenants exposes the leaders' rejection of God's Son.
He answers questions about taxes to Caesar, the resurrection, and the greatest commandment.
Jesus warns against the scribes and praises a poor widow's gift of two small coins.

13.line: On the Mount of Olives, Jesus foretells the temple's destruction, coming troubles, and his return.
more: He warns of false christs, wars, persecution, and the abomination of desolation.
The Son of Man will come in clouds and gather his elect.
Since no one knows the day or hour, his followers must stay awake.

14.line: Jesus is anointed, shares the Passover with his disciples, prays in Gethsemane, is arrested, and is tried.
more: Judas agrees to betray Jesus, who institutes the Lord's Supper with bread and cup.
In Gethsemane Jesus submits to the Father's will while the disciples sleep.
The council condemns him for claiming to be the Christ, and Peter denies him three times.

15.line: Pilate hands Jesus over to be crucified, and he dies on the cross and is buried.
more: The crowd chooses Barabbas, and soldiers mock Jesus as King of the Jews.
At Golgotha he is crucified between two robbers, and the temple curtain is torn.
A centurion calls him the Son of God, and Joseph of Arimathea buries him.

16.line: Women find Jesus' tomb empty and are told by a young man that Jesus has risen.
more: They are told to tell the disciples and Peter that Jesus goes ahead to Galilee.
The women flee from the tomb, trembling and afraid.
The longer ending found in many Bibles records resurrection appearances, a commission, and the ascension.

Luke.line: Luke gives an orderly account of Jesus' life, showing him as the Savior who seeks and saves the lost.
more: Luke writes to Theophilus, beginning with the births of John the Baptist and Jesus.
Jesus ministers in Galilee, teaching, healing, and calling disciples, with special concern for outsiders and the poor.
A long journey to Jerusalem contains many of his parables and teachings on discipleship.
In Jerusalem he is rejected, crucified, and buried.
He rises, appears to his disciples, explains the Scriptures, and ascends to heaven.

1.line: The angel Gabriel announces the births of John the Baptist and Jesus, and John is born.
more: Luke explains he is writing an orderly account for Theophilus.
Zechariah doubts Gabriel's message and is struck mute, while Mary accepts the news humbly.
Mary visits Elizabeth and praises God, and Zechariah prophesies at John's birth.

2.line: Jesus is born in Bethlehem, presented at the temple, and at twelve years old remains among the teachers there.
more: A Roman census brings Joseph and Mary to Bethlehem, where Jesus is laid in a manger.
Angels announce the birth to shepherds, who come and spread the news.
Simeon and Anna recognize the infant as the promised Savior in the temple.

3.line: John the Baptist preaches repentance, Jesus is baptized, and Jesus' genealogy is traced back to Adam.
more: John calls the crowds to bear fruit fitting repentance and announces a coming mightier one.
Herod imprisons John for rebuking him.
At Jesus' baptism the Spirit descends and the Father's voice calls him beloved Son.

4.line: Jesus resists the devil's temptations, is rejected at Nazareth, and heals and preaches in Galilee.
more: In the Nazareth synagogue he reads Isaiah and declares it fulfilled, and the people try to kill him.
In Capernaum he casts out a demon and heals Simon's mother-in-law and many others.
He continues preaching the kingdom of God in the synagogues.

5.line: Jesus calls his first disciples after a miraculous catch of fish and heals a leper and a paralyzed man.
more: Simon, James, and John leave everything to follow him.
Jesus forgives the paralytic's sins, provoking objections from scribes and Pharisees.
He calls Levi the tax collector and teaches about fasting and new wine.

6.line: Jesus defends his Sabbath actions, chooses the twelve apostles, and delivers the Sermon on the Plain.
more: Jesus heals a withered hand on the Sabbath, angering the scribes and Pharisees.
He pronounces blessings on the poor and woes on the rich and satisfied.
He teaches love for enemies, not judging others, and building on obedience to his words.

7.line: Jesus heals a centurion's servant, raises a widow's son, answers John's question, and forgives a sinful woman.
more: Jesus marvels at the Gentile centurion's faith.
He tells John's messengers to report the healings and good news to the poor.
At a Pharisee's house a sinful woman anoints his feet, and he says her faith has saved her.

8.line: Jesus teaches in parables, calms a storm, frees a demon-possessed man, and heals a woman and Jairus' daughter.
more: Several women, including Mary Magdalene, support his ministry.
The parable of the sower explains different responses to God's word.
He says his family are those who hear God's word and do it.

9.line: Jesus sends out the twelve, feeds five thousand, is confessed as the Christ, and is transfigured.
more: He foretells his death and teaches that disciples must take up their cross daily.
After the transfiguration he heals a boy and warns again of his betrayal.
He sets his face toward Jerusalem and describes the cost of following him.

10.line: Jesus sends out seventy-two messengers, tells the parable of the Good Samaritan, and visits Martha and Mary.
more: The seventy-two return rejoicing, and Jesus tells them to rejoice that their names are in heaven.
A lawyer's question about eternal life leads to the parable of a merciful Samaritan.
Jesus commends Mary for listening to his teaching while Martha is distracted with serving.

11.line: Jesus teaches about prayer, answers the charge of casting out demons by Beelzebul, and denounces the Pharisees.
more: He gives the Lord's Prayer and encourages persistent asking.
He says this generation will receive only the sign of Jonah.
Jesus pronounces woes on Pharisees and lawyers for hypocrisy, and they begin to oppose him fiercely.

12.line: Jesus warns against hypocrisy and greed, tells the parable of the rich fool, and urges readiness for his return.
more: He tells his disciples to fear God rather than people.
He teaches them not to be anxious but to seek God's kingdom.
He warns that he brings division and that people must read the signs of the times.

13.line: Jesus calls people to repent, heals a disabled woman on the Sabbath, and laments over Jerusalem.
more: The parable of the barren fig tree warns that time to bear fruit is limited.
Parables of the mustard seed and leaven describe the kingdom's growth.
He urges people to enter by the narrow door before it is shut.

14.line: At a Pharisee's dinner Jesus heals on the Sabbath and teaches about humility, hospitality, and the cost of discipleship.
more: He tells guests to take the lowest seat and hosts to invite the poor.
The parable of the great banquet shows invited guests refusing and outsiders brought in.
Disciples must count the cost and put Jesus above everything else.

15.line: Answering Pharisees who grumble about his welcome of sinners, Jesus tells three parables about the lost being found.
more: A shepherd finds a lost sheep, and a woman finds a lost coin, and both rejoice.
A father welcomes home his wasteful younger son with a celebration.
The older son resents the welcome, and the father urges him to rejoice.

16.line: Jesus teaches about the faithful use of money and tells the story of the rich man and Lazarus.
more: The parable of the dishonest manager leads to teaching that no one can serve God and money.
Jesus rebukes the money-loving Pharisees and affirms the lasting authority of the law.
After death the rich man suffers while Lazarus is comforted beside Abraham.

17.line: Jesus teaches about forgiveness, faith, and duty, heals ten lepers, and speaks of the coming of the Son of Man.
more: He warns against causing others to sin and calls for repeated forgiveness.
Only one of the ten healed lepers, a Samaritan, returns to thank him.
The Son of Man's day will come suddenly, as in the days of Noah and Lot.

18.line: Jesus teaches about prayer and humility, speaks with a rich ruler, foretells his death, and heals a blind beggar.
more: A persistent widow and a humble tax collector illustrate prayer that God hears.
Jesus welcomes children and warns that riches make entering the kingdom difficult.
Near Jericho a blind man calls to him and receives his sight.

19.line: Jesus saves Zacchaeus, tells the parable of the minas, enters Jerusalem, weeps over it, and cleanses the temple.
more: The tax collector Zacchaeus repents, and Jesus says he came to seek and save the lost.
The parable of the minas teaches faithful service until the king returns.
Disciples praise him on the descent from the Mount of Olives, and he foretells Jerusalem's destruction.

20.line: In the temple religious leaders challenge Jesus' authority and try to trap him with questions.
more: The parable of the wicked tenants condemns the leaders who reject God's Son.
He answers questions about paying taxes to Caesar and about the resurrection.
Jesus asks how the Christ can be David's son and warns against the scribes.

21.line: Jesus praises a widow's offering and foretells the temple's destruction, coming distress, and his return.
more: He warns of false messiahs, wars, persecution, and Jerusalem surrounded by armies.
The Son of Man will come in a cloud with power and great glory.
He tells his disciples to stay awake and pray.

22.line: Jesus shares the Last Supper, prays on the Mount of Olives, is betrayed by Judas, and is denied by Peter.
more: Judas agrees with the chief priests to hand Jesus over.
Jesus gives bread and cup as a new covenant in his blood and rebukes the disciples' quarrel about greatness.
After his arrest he is mocked, and the council questions him about being the Son of God.

23.line: Jesus is tried before Pilate and Herod, crucified between two criminals, dies, and is buried.
more: Pilate finds no guilt in Jesus but yields to the crowd and releases Barabbas.
Jesus prays for forgiveness for his executioners and promises paradise to a repentant criminal.
Joseph of Arimathea lays his body in a new tomb.

24.line: Jesus rises from the dead, appears to his disciples, explains the Scriptures, and ascends to heaven.
more: Women find the tomb empty, and angels tell them Jesus has risen.
On the road to Emmaus, Jesus explains how the Scriptures point to him.
He commissions the disciples to proclaim repentance and forgiveness and to wait for power from on high.

John.line: John presents Jesus as the eternal Word made flesh, so that readers may believe he is the Christ.
more: John opens by declaring that the Word who was God became flesh.
Jesus performs signs and gives discourses revealing who he is, provoking both belief and opposition.
The raising of Lazarus leads the leaders to plan Jesus' death.
On his last night Jesus washes his disciples' feet, teaches them, and prays for them.
He is crucified, rises from the dead, and appears to his disciples.

1.line: The eternal Word becomes flesh, John the Baptist testifies about him, and Jesus calls his first disciples.
more: The Word was with God, was God, and made all things.
John the Baptist identifies Jesus as the Lamb of God who takes away sin.
Andrew, Peter, Philip, and Nathanael begin following Jesus.

2.line: Jesus turns water into wine at a wedding in Cana and drives the money-changers from the temple.
more: The Cana miracle is his first sign, and his disciples believe in him.
He tells the Jews that if this temple is destroyed he will raise it in three days.
After his resurrection the disciples understand he spoke of his body.

3.line: Jesus tells Nicodemus that one must be born again, and John the Baptist testifies that Jesus must increase.
more: Jesus explains that birth by the Spirit is needed to enter God's kingdom.
God gave his Son so that whoever believes in him has eternal life.
John the Baptist calls himself the friend of the bridegroom.

4.line: Jesus offers living water to a Samaritan woman, many Samaritans believe, and he heals an official's son.
more: Jesus reveals knowledge of the woman's life and declares himself the Messiah.
He teaches that true worshipers worship the Father in spirit and truth.
In Cana he heals the official's son at a distance, his second sign.

5.line: Jesus heals a disabled man on the Sabbath and defends his authority as the Son equal with the Father.
more: The man had been ill thirty-eight years and lay by the pool of Bethesda.
Jewish leaders seek to kill Jesus for calling God his own Father.
Jesus cites the witness of John, his works, the Father, and Moses' writings.

6.line: Jesus feeds five thousand, walks on the sea, and teaches that he is the bread of life.
more: The crowd wants to make him king, but he withdraws.
He says those who eat his flesh and drink his blood have eternal life.
Many disciples leave, but Peter says Jesus has the words of eternal life.

7.line: At the Feast of Booths Jesus teaches in the temple, causing division over who he is.
more: His brothers do not believe in him, and he goes up to the feast privately.
He invites the thirsty to come to him and promises rivers of living water.
Officers sent to arrest him return without him, and Nicodemus urges a fair hearing.

8.line: Jesus declares he is the light of the world and claims existence before Abraham, and opponents try to stone him.
more: The account of a woman caught in adultery, bracketed in many Bibles, appears at the chapter's opening.
Jesus says the truth will set free those who abide in his word.
He tells his opponents they act as children of the devil, not of Abraham.

9.line: Jesus heals a man born blind, and the Pharisees investigate and expel the man from the synagogue.
more: Jesus says the man's blindness was so God's works might be displayed.
The man's parents fear the leaders, but the man boldly defends Jesus.
Jesus reveals himself to the man, who worships him, and speaks of spiritual blindness.

10.line: Jesus calls himself the good shepherd who lays down his life, and at the Feast of Dedication claims oneness with the Father.
more: His sheep hear his voice, and no one can snatch them from his hand.
His opponents try to stone him for blasphemy and then to arrest him.
He withdraws across the Jordan, where many believe in him.

11.line: Jesus raises Lazarus from the dead, and the Jewish council resolves to put Jesus to death.
more: Jesus tells Martha he is the resurrection and the life.
He weeps at the tomb and calls Lazarus out after four days.
Caiaphas says one man should die for the people, and the council plots.

12.line: Mary anoints Jesus at Bethany, he enters Jerusalem in triumph, and he speaks of his coming death.
more: Judas objects to the costly perfume, and the leaders plot against Lazarus too.
When Greeks seek him, Jesus compares his death to a grain of wheat that dies.
Many still do not believe, fulfilling Isaiah's words, though some leaders believe secretly.

13.line: At supper Jesus washes his disciples' feet, foretells Judas' betrayal, and gives a new commandment to love.
more: Jesus tells them to wash one another's feet, following his example.
Judas receives the morsel and goes out into the night.
Jesus foretells that Peter will deny him three times.

14.line: Jesus comforts his disciples, declaring he is the way to the Father and promising the Holy Spirit.
more: He goes to prepare a place for them and will come again.
Whoever has seen Jesus has seen the Father.
Those who love him will keep his commandments, and he leaves them his peace.

15.line: Jesus calls himself the true vine, commands his disciples to love one another, and warns of the world's hatred.
more: Branches that abide in him bear much fruit, while fruitless branches are removed.
No one has greater love than one who lays down his life for friends.
The Spirit and the disciples will bear witness about him.

16.line: Jesus explains the Spirit's coming work and foretells that the disciples' sorrow will turn to joy.
more: The Spirit will convict the world and guide the disciples into all truth.
After a little while they will see him again.
He tells them they will have tribulation, but he has overcome the world.

17.line: Jesus prays to the Father for his own glorification, for his disciples, and for all future believers.
more: He has finished the work the Father gave him and asks to be glorified.
He asks the Father to keep the disciples and sanctify them in the truth.
He prays that all believers may be one so the world may believe.

18.line: Jesus is arrested, questioned before Annas and Caiaphas, denied by Peter, and examined by Pilate.
more: In the garden Peter cuts off the ear of the high priest's servant.
Jesus tells Pilate his kingdom is not of this world.
Pilate finds no guilt, but the crowd demands Barabbas instead.

19.line: Pilate hands Jesus over, and he is crucified, dies, and is buried by Joseph and Nicodemus.
more: Soldiers flog Jesus and crown him with thorns, and the crowd shouts for crucifixion.
On the cross he entrusts his mother to the beloved disciple and declares it finished.
A soldier pierces his side, and his legs are not broken, fulfilling Scripture.

20.line: Jesus' tomb is found empty, and the risen Jesus appears to Mary Magdalene, the disciples, and Thomas.
more: Peter and the beloved disciple run to the tomb and see the grave cloths.
Jesus breathes on the disciples and says to receive the Holy Spirit.
Thomas confesses him as Lord and God, and John states his purpose in writing.

21.line: The risen Jesus appears by the Sea of Tiberias, provides a great catch, and restores Peter.
more: The disciples catch one hundred fifty-three fish and share breakfast with Jesus.
Three times Jesus asks Peter if he loves him and tells him to feed his sheep.
Jesus foretells Peter's death, and the beloved disciple is identified as the book's witness.

Acts.line: Acts records how the apostles, empowered by the Holy Spirit, spread the gospel from Jerusalem to Rome.
more: Jesus ascends, and the Spirit comes at Pentecost, birthing the church in Jerusalem.
Persecution after Stephen's death scatters believers, and the gospel reaches Samaria.
Saul is converted, and Peter's visit to Cornelius opens the church to Gentiles.
Paul's missionary journeys plant churches across Asia Minor and Greece.
Paul is arrested in Jerusalem, appeals to Caesar, and preaches in Rome under guard.

1.line: Jesus promises the Holy Spirit, ascends to heaven, and the apostles choose Matthias to replace Judas.
more: Jesus appears to the apostles for forty days, speaking about God's kingdom.
They will be his witnesses in Jerusalem, Judea, Samaria, and to the end of the earth.
The believers pray together, and lots fall on Matthias.

2.line: At Pentecost the Holy Spirit fills the believers, Peter preaches, and about three thousand are baptized.
more: The disciples speak in other languages, and visitors hear God's works in their own tongues.
Peter proclaims that God raised Jesus and made him Lord and Christ.
The believers devote themselves to teaching, fellowship, breaking bread, prayer, and sharing.

3.line: Peter and John heal a lame man at the temple gate, and Peter preaches to the gathered crowd.
more: The man walks and leaps, praising God, and the people are astonished.
Peter credits faith in Jesus' name for the healing.
He calls the people to repent so that their sins may be blotted out.

4.line: Peter and John are arrested, boldly testify before the council, and are released with warnings.
more: Peter declares there is salvation in no other name than Jesus.
The believers pray for boldness, and the place where they gather is shaken.
They share possessions, and Barnabas sells a field and gives the money.

5.line: Ananias and Sapphira die for lying to the Holy Spirit, and the apostles are imprisoned, freed, and beaten.
more: Many signs and healings are done through the apostles.
An angel frees them, and they resume teaching in the temple.
Gamaliel advises the council to leave them alone, and they rejoice after being flogged.

6.line: Seven men are chosen to serve the widows, and Stephen is seized and falsely accused.
more: Hellenist believers complain their widows are neglected in the daily distribution.
The apostles devote themselves to prayer and the ministry of the word.
Stephen does great wonders, and opponents charge him with blasphemy against Moses and the temple.

7.line: Stephen recounts Israel's history before the council and is stoned to death.
more: He describes how Israel repeatedly resisted God's messengers, from Joseph to Moses.
He accuses his hearers of resisting the Holy Spirit and killing the Righteous One.
He sees Jesus at God's right hand, prays for his killers, and Saul approves.

8.line: Persecution scatters the church, and Philip preaches in Samaria and to an Ethiopian official.
more: Saul ravages the church, entering houses and dragging believers to prison.
Samaritans believe, and Peter and John come so they receive the Spirit.
Simon the magician tries to buy the Spirit's power and is rebuked.

9.line: The risen Jesus confronts Saul on the Damascus road, and Saul is converted and begins preaching.
more: Saul is blinded, and Ananias lays hands on him so he regains sight.
Saul escapes a plot by being lowered in a basket, and Barnabas vouches for him.
Peter heals Aeneas at Lydda and raises Tabitha at Joppa.

10.line: God leads Peter to the Roman centurion Cornelius, and the Holy Spirit falls on Gentiles who hear the gospel.
more: An angel tells Cornelius to send for Peter.
Peter's vision of unclean animals teaches him not to call people unclean.
Peter preaches that God shows no partiality, and the Gentile believers are baptized.

11.line: Peter explains Gentile conversion to the Jerusalem church, and a church grows in Antioch.
more: The Jerusalem believers glorify God that Gentiles have been granted repentance.
Barnabas brings Saul to Antioch, where disciples are first called Christians.
The Antioch church sends famine relief to Judea.

12.line: Herod kills James and imprisons Peter, but an angel frees Peter, and Herod later dies.
more: The church prays earnestly while Peter is in prison.
Peter arrives at Mary's house, and Rhoda is too excited to open the gate.
Herod accepts praise as a god and is struck down, while the word spreads.

13.line: The Antioch church sends Barnabas and Saul on mission to Cyprus and Pisidian Antioch.
more: On Cyprus a sorcerer is blinded, and the proconsul believes.
Paul preaches in the synagogue that forgiveness comes through the risen Jesus.
When Jews oppose them, they turn to the Gentiles and are driven out.

14.line: Paul and Barnabas preach in Iconium, Lystra, and Derbe, then return to strengthen the churches.
more: At Lystra Paul heals a lame man, and the crowd tries to worship them as gods.
Opponents stone Paul and leave him for dead, but he rises and continues.
They appoint elders and report to Antioch how God opened a door to Gentiles.

15.line: The Jerusalem council decides Gentile believers need not be circumcised, and Paul and Barnabas separate.
more: Peter testifies that God saves Jews and Gentiles alike by grace.
James proposes a few requirements, sent by letter to the Gentile churches.
Paul and Barnabas disagree over John Mark, and Paul departs with Silas.

16.line: Paul is called to Macedonia, where Lydia believes and a Philippian jailer is saved after an earthquake.
more: Timothy joins Paul, and a vision of a Macedonian man directs their route.
Paul casts a spirit out of a slave girl, and her owners have him and Silas beaten and jailed.
Paul and Silas, as Roman citizens, receive a public apology before leaving.

17.line: Paul preaches in Thessalonica, Berea, and Athens, where he addresses the Areopagus.
more: In Thessalonica jealous Jews start a riot and drag Jason before the authorities.
The Bereans examine the Scriptures daily to test Paul's message.
In Athens Paul proclaims the unknown God as Creator and Judge who raised Jesus.

18.line: Paul ministers in Corinth for eighteen months, then returns to Antioch, while Apollos teaches in Ephesus.
more: Paul works with Aquila and Priscilla as a tentmaker and preaches in the synagogue.
The Lord tells Paul in a vision not to fear, and Gallio dismisses charges against him.
Priscilla and Aquila explain the way of God more accurately to Apollos.

19.line: Paul ministers two years in Ephesus, the word spreads widely, and a riot breaks out over the goddess Artemis.
more: Disciples who knew only John's baptism are baptized in Jesus' name and receive the Spirit.
After the sons of Sceva are overpowered by a demon, many burn their magic books.
The silversmith Demetrius incites the crowd, but the town clerk disperses it.

20.line: Paul travels through Macedonia and Greece, raises Eutychus at Troas, and bids farewell to the Ephesian elders.
more: Eutychus falls from a window during Paul's long sermon and is restored to life.
At Miletus Paul recounts his ministry and warns of false teachers.
He charges the elders to shepherd the church, and they weep at parting.

21.line: Despite warnings, Paul goes to Jerusalem, where he is seized in the temple and arrested by Roman soldiers.
more: Agabus binds his own hands and feet with Paul's belt to foretell Paul's arrest.
James and the elders ask Paul to join others in a purification rite.
Jews from Asia stir up the crowd, and the tribune rescues Paul from being killed.

22.line: Paul tells the Jerusalem crowd of his conversion, and his Roman citizenship spares him from flogging.
more: He describes his zeal, his encounter with Jesus, and Ananias' role.
The crowd erupts when Paul says the Lord sent him to the Gentiles.
The tribune brings Paul before the council to learn the charges.

23.line: Paul divides the council, a plot against his life is uncovered, and he is sent to Governor Felix.
more: Paul declares he is on trial for the hope of the resurrection, splitting Pharisees and Sadducees.
The Lord tells Paul he must testify in Rome.
Paul's nephew reports the plot, and soldiers escort Paul to Caesarea by night.

24.line: Paul defends himself before Felix, who delays a decision and keeps him in custody for two years.
more: The lawyer Tertullus accuses Paul of stirring riots and profaning the temple.
Paul denies the charges and affirms his hope in the resurrection.
Felix hears Paul speak on righteousness and judgment but hopes for a bribe.

25.line: Before the new governor Festus, Paul appeals to Caesar, and King Agrippa arrives to hear his case.
more: Jewish leaders press charges they cannot prove.
Paul refuses to be tried in Jerusalem and appeals to Caesar.
Festus seeks Agrippa's help in stating charges for Rome.

26.line: Paul recounts his conversion and commission to King Agrippa, who judges him innocent.
more: Jesus sent Paul to open the Gentiles' eyes and turn them from darkness to light.
Festus calls Paul mad, and Paul urges Agrippa to believe.
Agrippa says Paul could have been freed had he not appealed to Caesar.

27.line: Paul sails as a prisoner toward Rome, and after a violent storm the ship wrecks but all survive.
more: Paul warns against sailing, but the centurion follows the pilot and owner.
An angel assures Paul that everyone aboard will be saved.
The ship runs aground near an island, and all 276 people reach land.

28.line: On Malta Paul survives a viper's bite and heals the sick, then reaches Rome and preaches there.
more: Paul heals the father of Publius, the island's chief official, and others.
In Rome he explains the kingdom and Jesus to Jewish leaders, some of whom believe.
For two years under guard he preaches boldly and without hindrance.

Romans.line: Paul's letter to the church in Rome explains the gospel of God's righteousness received by faith in Jesus Christ.
more: Paul shows that all people, Jews and Gentiles, are under sin and condemned.
God justifies sinners freely by grace through faith in Christ, as he did Abraham.
Believers are freed from sin's dominion and live by the Spirit with sure hope.
Paul explains God's faithfulness to Israel and his plan for Jews and Gentiles.
He describes how the gospel shapes life together and closes with plans and greetings.

1.line: Paul introduces the gospel as God's power for salvation and shows God's wrath against humanity's rejection of him.
more: Paul greets the Roman believers and expresses his longing to visit them.
In the gospel God's righteousness is revealed by faith.
People suppress the truth and worship idols, so God gives them over to sin.

2.line: Paul argues that those who judge others, including Jews with the law, are also guilty before God.
more: God judges everyone impartially according to their deeds.
Having the law does not save those who break it.
True circumcision is a matter of the heart, by the Spirit.

3.line: All people are under sin, but God's righteousness is given through faith in Christ apart from the law.
more: Jews were entrusted with God's words, yet God remains faithful despite their unfaithfulness.
Scripture shows that no one is righteous, and the law brings knowledge of sin.
God justifies freely by grace through Christ's sacrifice as a propitiation, excluding boasting.

4.line: Paul shows that Abraham was counted righteous through faith, not works or circumcision.
more: David also speaks of the blessing of sins forgiven apart from works.
Abraham was counted righteous before he was circumcised, making him father of all who believe.
Righteousness will be counted to all who believe in God who raised Jesus.

5.line: Justified by faith, believers have peace with God, and Christ's obedience overcomes the sin brought by Adam.
more: Believers rejoice in hope, even in suffering, because God's love is poured into their hearts.
Christ died for the ungodly while they were still sinners.
Sin and death came through Adam, but grace and life abound through Christ.

6.line: Paul argues that believers, united with Christ in his death and resurrection, must no longer live in sin.
more: Baptism into Christ signifies dying to sin and rising to new life.
Believers are to present themselves to God as instruments of righteousness.
The wages of sin is death, but God's gift is eternal life.

7.line: Paul explains that believers are released from the law, which is holy but cannot overcome sin.
more: As death ends a marriage, death with Christ frees believers to belong to him.
Sin uses the commandment to produce death, though the law itself is good.
Paul describes an inner struggle of wanting to do good yet doing evil, and thanks God for deliverance.

8.line: There is no condemnation for those in Christ, who live by the Spirit and are secure in God's love.
more: The Spirit gives life and testifies that believers are God's adopted children.
Creation groans awaiting redemption, and the Spirit intercedes for believers in weakness.
God works all things for good, and nothing can separate believers from his love.

9.line: Grieving over Israel's unbelief, Paul explains that God's promises depend on his sovereign mercy, not human descent.
more: Not all descended from Israel belong to Israel; God chose Isaac and Jacob.
God has mercy on whom he wills, as with Pharaoh and the potter's clay.
Gentiles attain righteousness by faith, while Israel stumbles by pursuing it through works.

10.line: Paul explains that righteousness comes by faith in Christ, and Israel has heard the message but not believed.
more: Israel sought to establish its own righteousness, but Christ is the end of the law for righteousness.
Everyone who confesses Jesus as Lord and believes God raised him will be saved.
People must hear to believe, so preachers must be sent.

11.line: God has not rejected Israel; their stumbling brings salvation to Gentiles, and all Israel will be saved.
more: A remnant of Israel is chosen by grace, as in Elijah's day.
Gentiles are like wild branches grafted into an olive tree and must not be proud.
Paul closes with praise for the depth of God's wisdom and knowledge.

12.line: Paul urges believers to offer themselves to God as living sacrifices and to live in sincere love.
more: Believers are to be transformed by the renewal of their minds.
As one body, they use their different gifts to serve one another.
They are to bless persecutors, avoid revenge, and overcome evil with good.

13.line: Paul instructs believers to submit to governing authorities and to love others, since salvation is near.
more: Rulers are instituted by God, so believers pay taxes and give respect.
Love fulfills the law because it does no wrong to a neighbor.
Believers are to cast off works of darkness and put on the Lord Jesus Christ.

14.line: Paul teaches believers who differ over food and special days not to judge one another or cause stumbling.
more: Each believer lives to the Lord and will give account to God.
The kingdom of God is about righteousness, peace, and joy, not food and drink.
The strong should give up their liberty rather than harm a weaker believer.

15.line: Paul calls believers to welcome one another as Christ welcomed them, and shares his ministry and travel plans.
more: Christ served the Jews so that Gentiles also might glorify God for his mercy.
Paul describes his calling to preach where Christ has not been named.
He plans to deliver aid to Jerusalem, then visit Rome on his way to Spain.

16.line: Paul commends Phoebe, greets many believers in Rome, warns against divisive teachers, and closes with praise to God.
more: He sends greetings to Prisca, Aquila, and many other coworkers and friends.
He urges the church to avoid those who cause divisions contrary to sound teaching.
Timothy and others send greetings, and Paul ends with a doxology.
